title: Construction Site Safety Compliance
summary: Use site cameras and safety walk photos to spot missing helmets, unguarded edges, people in crane and hoist zones and poor housekeeping, with each observation verified by the safety officer.

seo.title: Construction Site Safety Compliance with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision for construction sites: PPE checks, crane and edge zone alerts and housekeeping observations, reviewed by your safety officer.

problem.intro: A high-rise site changes every day: new slab edges, openings, crane lifts and subcontractor crews. Safety officers cannot be on every floor, and observations from safety walks are written up later, so many unsafe acts come to light only after an incident or an inspection.

pain_points.title: Too much site for too few eyes
pain_points.detail: One or two safety officers cover several towers, crane operations and night shifts, and rely on supervisors to report issues.

pain_points.title: Edge and opening protection that comes and goes
pain_points.detail: Barricades, guardrails and shaft covers are removed for work and not replaced, especially on newly cast slabs.

pain_points.title: PPE compliance that drops off
pain_points.detail: Helmets and high-visibility jackets are worn at the gate and taken off on upper floors or during breaks.

pain_points.title: Observations that do not lead to action
pain_points.detail: Safety walk findings sit in notebooks or WhatsApp, so repeat issues by contractor or area are hard to track and close.

solution.overview: We build a safety monitoring system on your existing site cameras and safety walk photos. Vision models check for helmets and high-visibility jackets, people inside marked crane swing, hoist and excavation zones, missing edge protection at marked slab edges and openings, and blocked access routes or debris. Each detection becomes an observation with a snapshot, location and confidence. Urgent detections, such as a person under a suspended load, alert the safety officer immediately; the rest go into a review queue. Confirmed observations are assigned to the responsible contractor, tracked to closure and summarised daily by area and contractor.
capabilities: Helmet and high-visibility jacket detection on CCTV and photos
Zone rules for crane swing areas, hoist landings and excavation edges
Checks for missing guardrails or covers at marked slab edges and openings
Housekeeping observations for debris, material blocking access and waterlogging
Observation tracking by contractor and area, with photo evidence through to closure
Daily and weekly safety summaries for toolbox talks and review meetings

workflow.title: Map cameras and zones
workflow.detail: We map existing cameras, mark crane, hoist, edge and excavation zones and agree observation types with the EHS team.

workflow.title: Analyse feeds and photos
workflow.detail: Camera frames and safety walk photos are analysed at agreed intervals for PPE, zone and housekeeping issues.

workflow.title: Score severity
workflow.detail: Each detection gets a severity and confidence score, and critical zone breaches trigger an immediate alert.

workflow.title: Safety officer review
workflow.detail: The safety officer confirms or dismisses observations from the queue using the snapshot and location.

workflow.title: Assign and close
workflow.detail: Confirmed observations go to the responsible contractor supervisor, who closes them with a photo.

workflow.title: Report trends
workflow.detail: Daily and weekly summaries show repeat issues by area, shift and contractor for toolbox talks and reviews.

inputs: Site layout with crane, hoist and excavation zones
outputs: Immediate alerts for critical zone breaches
Observation records with snapshot, location and severity
human_in_the_loop: The safety officer confirms every observation before it is assigned, and decides any penalty or stop-work action under your site rules. Immediate alerts prompt a person to check; they never stop work automatically.
integrations: CCTV network video recorders over RTSP
WhatsApp or SMS for alerts to site teams
guardrails: No face recognition; detections concern PPE and zones, not identity
Faces blurred in reports shared outside the safety team
Penalties and stop-work decisions stay with authorised staff
Zone maps reviewed weekly as the site layout changes
Alert thresholds tuned to avoid alarm fatigue
compliance_notes: Helps evidence site safety practices expected under the BOCW Act 1996 and the OSH Code 2020; it does not replace statutory inspections.
Worker images are handled with notice, restricted access and retention limits in line with the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One tower or work zone with three to six existing cameras plus daily safety walk photos, with detections reviewed by the site safety officer.
deliverables: Camera and zone map for the pilot area
PPE, zone and housekeeping detection tuned on site footage
Pilot observation log and weekly summaries

what_we_measure.how: Share of detections the safety officer confirms as genuine.
Observations the safety officer records on walks in covered areas that the system did not flag.
Time from confirmation to closure photo, compared with the existing observation register.
Count of alerts and dismissals, used to tune thresholds.

faqs.q: Can we use our existing CCTV cameras?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if they cover the areas that matter at reasonable resolution. During setup we review each camera's view and suggest where one should be moved or added, for example to cover a hoist landing or crane loading area.
No. The system detects PPE and zone breaches, not who the person is. Faces can be blurred in reports, and access to raw footage stays with your safety team.
Where lighting and cameras support it. Night footage is noisier, so thresholds are set separately and more items go to review. Poorly lit work areas are themselves worth flagging.

faqs.q: Can it detect whether fall-arrest gear is being used?
faqs.a: Safety belts and lanyards are hard to see reliably from fixed cameras, so we treat them as a review prompt rather than a dependable detection. Edge protection and zone rules usually give stronger signals.
